intro.eyebrow: A field guide to the worlds we play
intro.description: Every adventurer enters a world for a different reason. Follow your instincts through 30 choices and discover what makes your kind of play.
intro.footnote: No wrong answers. Just your way of playing.

test.prompt: Two paths open before you. Which one feels like yours?
test.crossroadsDescription: A traveler stands at a crossroads with two paths ahead.
test.keyboardHint: Press 1 or 2 to choose a path.

results.title: The path you make
results.description: There’s no single way to belong in a world. Here’s what your choices say about yours.
results.scoreNote: Each choice adds one point to a player type. Percentages show how your choices were distributed.
results.copyError: Could not copy the result. Please try again.
results.acknowledgement: Inspired by Richard Bartle’s player-type taxonomy and the referenced Bartle test. This version uses an original set of questions.

socialiser.name: Socialiser
socialiser.description: For you, the world comes alive through its people. Shared stories, familiar faces, and the bonds built along the way are the real adventure.

explorer.name: Explorer
explorer.description: You play to discover what lies beyond the obvious. Hidden details, untold histories, and the joy of understanding a world pull you forward.

achiever.name: Achiever
achiever.description: A clear goal gives your journey meaning. You enjoy mastering a challenge, earning progress, and seeing how far dedication can take you.

killer.name: Killer
killer.description: You thrive on impact and high-stakes encounters. Competition is compelling, and you enjoy testing your skill against another player.

about.description: Bartle’s taxonomy describes four reasons people are drawn to multiplayer worlds: people, discovery, accomplishment, and competition. Most players are a blend.
